group.name: Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center Receiver
group.description: Dashboard group for Cisco Secure Firewall Management Center API trust, managed firewall health, interfaces, VPN, HA, policy, deployment, and audit metrics emitted by the Cisco OS receiver.

variables.description: Secure Firewall Management Center controller name.
Managed firewall, chassis, interface, or FMC object name.
Managed Secure Firewall or chassis serial number.
Managed firewall or chassis interface name.
FMC policy name when the source object provides one.
FMC domain UUID used for scoped API requests.

dashboards.name: 00 FMC API Trust And Fleet
dashboards.description: First-response dashboard for FMC reachability, scrape completeness, API behavior, managed-firewall availability, and collection coverage.
dashboards.value: Proves whether FMC collection is trustworthy and which managed firewalls are affected before ITOps or NetOps act on health, interface, VPN, HA, policy, or deployment symptoms.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use FMC management-plane telemetry as the incident starting point. Interpretation: prove controller reachability, scrape completeness, freshness, and endpoint coverage before treating missing firewall evidence as a network outage.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Start here for Cisco Secure Firewall incidents. Confirm that each FMC controller is reachable, the scrape is complete and fresh, and API errors or rate limits are not hiding data. Then use managed-firewall availability and inventory coverage to identify the affected scope before moving to the health, VPN/HA, or policy/deployment dashboards.

charts.name: FMC Manager Availability
charts.description: Value: shows whether each configured FMC REST API was available during the scrape. Interpretation: 0 points to controller reachability, authentication, token, TLS, or API availability trouble rather than managed-firewall state.

charts.name: FMC Scrape Partial Success
charts.description: Value: shows whether one or more FMC endpoint families failed during collection. Interpretation: 1 means downstream panels may be incomplete; inspect endpoint-family errors before concluding that objects disappeared.

charts.name: Last Fully Successful Scrape
charts.description: Value: shows the Unix timestamp of the most recent fully successful FMC scrape. Interpretation: a flat or old value while partial success remains 1 means the dashboard is retaining stale success evidence rather than proving current collection health.

charts.name: FMC API Request Errors
charts.description: Value: counts failed FMC REST requests by controller, operation, HTTP status, and outcome. Interpretation: rising errors isolate token, permission, endpoint, release-compatibility, or server failures that can make individual dashboards incomplete.

charts.name: FMC Endpoint Family Errors
charts.description: Value: identifies the exact FMC endpoint family that failed while other data remained available. Interpretation: use operation and error kind to distinguish a narrow unsupported or unauthorized API from a controller-wide outage.

charts.name: FMC API Request Duration
charts.description: Value: tracks average FMC REST request duration by controller, operation, and outcome. Interpretation: sustained latency can consume the scrape timeout and precede partial collection or stale incident evidence.

charts.name: FMC API Rate Limiting
charts.description: Value: counts FMC REST requests that were rate limited. Interpretation: repeated non-zero values mean collection interval, page size, enabled groups, or target scope should be reduced before telemetry becomes stale.

charts.name: Managed Firewall Availability
charts.description: Value: shows FMC-reported availability for managed firewall inventory objects. Interpretation: 0 indicates a managed device symptom after FMC collection trust has been established; group by device and serial to identify the blast radius.

charts.name: FMC Fleet And Manager Coverage
charts.description: Value: counts manager and inventory objects by endpoint operation, resource type, and status. Interpretation: sudden count changes can reveal inventory scope, permission, API compatibility, device replacement, or collection regressions.

dashboards.name: 01 Firewall Interface And Health
dashboards.description: Managed-firewall troubleshooting dashboard for device availability, interface state, FMC health evidence, and inventory/interface/health object coverage.
dashboards.value: Helps NetOps separate a firewall outage, failed interface, chassis symptom, and health alarm from an FMC collection problem.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to correlate managed-firewall, interface, and health evidence. Interpretation: start with device and interface state, then use health status, event counts, and resource coverage to identify the affected object and likely failure domain.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard after the FMC API trust page is healthy. It connects FMC-reported firewall availability and interface state with health alerts, events, aggregate health objects, chassis evidence, and endpoint-family coverage so ITOps and NetOps can isolate the failed device, interface, or subsystem.

charts.name: Firewall Availability By Device
charts.description: Value: lists FMC-managed firewalls that are up or down. Interpretation: a transition to 0 after collection trust remains healthy identifies a device-side availability event that should be correlated with health and interface state.

charts.name: Managed Firewall Interface Status
charts.description: Value: shows FMC-reported operational state for physical, logical, bridge-group, EtherChannel, VNI, and chassis interfaces. Interpretation: failed or degraded rows identify the device and interface path to investigate before blaming policy or upstream routing.

charts.name: FMC Health Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded status for health alerts, events, path monitors, and aggregate CPU, memory, interface, disk, or chassis health objects. Interpretation: non-healthy rows identify the affected device, operation, severity, and resource type.

charts.name: FMC Health Events
charts.description: Value: counts recent FMC health alerts and health-related objects by operation, resource type, status, and severity. Interpretation: spikes near an outage window show whether device, interface, disk, chassis, CPU, or memory evidence changed with user impact.

charts.name: Interface And Health Resource Status
charts.description: Value: provides one exception list across FMC interface and health managed objects. Interpretation: use resource type, operation, status, and host to move from a broad health symptom to the exact object family that changed.

charts.name: Interface And Health Collection Coverage
charts.description: Value: counts interface and health objects returned by FMC. Interpretation: sudden drops to zero or large count changes can indicate target filtering, permissions, unsupported endpoints, device replacement, or a collection regression rather than an operational recovery.

dashboards.name: 02 VPN And HA Availability
dashboards.description: Availability dashboard for site-to-site and remote-access VPN state, FMC/FTD HA pairs, clusters, monitored interfaces, and failover posture.
dashboards.value: Shows whether an outage is caused by a VPN tunnel or gateway symptom, an HA/failover problem, or missing FMC coverage for those object families.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to use VPN and HA evidence during perimeter or remote-access incidents. Interpretation: find failed tunnel, gateway, pair, cluster, or monitored-interface state, then verify that matching object coverage did not disappear because of API or permission gaps.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard for site-to-site VPN, remote-access VPN, firewall failover, or cluster incidents. Current tunnel and HA state are shown as exception-friendly lists; adjacent coverage charts prove whether the expected FMC endpoint families returned objects during the incident window.

charts.name: VPN Tunnel And Gateway Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded status for VPN tunnels, tunnel details, summaries, remote-access gateways, and VPN policies. Interpretation: failed or degraded rows identify the controller, object, operation, and original VPN state behind connectivity impact.

charts.name: VPN Object Coverage
charts.description: Value: counts VPN tunnel, gateway, policy, summary, and detail objects returned by FMC. Interpretation: unexpected count loss can indicate target scope, permissions, release differences, or endpoint failure instead of real tunnel recovery.

charts.name: FMC And Firewall HA Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded FMC HA, FTD HA-pair, cluster, monitored-interface, and failover state. Interpretation: degraded rows reveal lost redundancy or monitored-link failure even when the active firewall remains reachable.

charts.name: HA Object Coverage
charts.description: Value: counts FMC HA, FTD pair, cluster, and monitored-interface objects by operation and status. Interpretation: compare count changes with HA state to distinguish an actual topology change from missing API coverage.

charts.name: VPN And HA Resource Exceptions
charts.description: Value: combines generic managed-object status for VPN and HA endpoint families. Interpretation: use this list when a product-specific status chart is empty or when policy, gateway, pair, cluster, and monitored-interface states need one correlated exception queue.

dashboards.name: 03 Policy Deployment And Change Evidence
dashboards.description: Change-correlation dashboard for FMC policy objects and rules, deployment state and backlog, audit records, and configuration changes.
dashboards.value: Helps incident responders determine whether policy drift, an undeployed change, a failed deployment, or an administrative action preceded firewall impact.

charts.name: Value Provided
charts.description: Value: explains how to correlate policy, deployment, and audit evidence during incident autopsy. Interpretation: compare object counts and status with deployment backlog and audit activity to decide whether a management-plane change plausibly caused user impact.
charts.markdown:
## Value Provided
Use this dashboard when connectivity, inspection, NAT, segmentation, or security behavior changed after an FMC policy action. Policy and rule coverage shows what FMC returned, deployment state exposes failed or pending rollout, and audit/config-change counts place administrative activity on the incident timeline. Use the logs pipeline for the full high-cardinality audit and change records.

charts.name: Policy Object And Rule Coverage
charts.description: Value: counts access, prefilter, NAT, intrusion, file, DNS, decryption, health, platform, security-intelligence, zone, SGT, application, and related policy objects and rules. Interpretation: unexpected count changes identify the policy family to inspect for drift or collection gaps.

charts.name: Policy Resource Status
charts.description: Value: lists encoded status for policy, rule, object, security-zone, SGT, syslog, and security-intelligence resources. Interpretation: failed or degraded rows identify the controller, policy, object family, and operation most likely to explain changed enforcement.

charts.name: Deployment Status
charts.description: Value: shows encoded status for deployable devices, deployment jobs, pending changes, and device deployment records. Interpretation: failed, waiting, or incomplete state indicates that intended policy may not match the running firewall configuration.

charts.name: Deployment Backlog
charts.description: Value: counts deployable devices, deployment jobs, pending changes, and device deployment objects by status. Interpretation: sustained or growing pending/failed counts indicate configuration drift or a rollout blocked before reaching managed firewalls.

charts.name: Audit And Configuration Change Evidence
charts.description: Value: counts recent FMC audit and configuration-change records by operation, status, and severity. Interpretation: spikes near the incident window identify management-plane activity to correlate with the detailed FMC logs without putting usernames or raw change text into metric dimensions.

charts.name: Policy Deployment And Audit Coverage
charts.description: Value: compares object volume across policy, deployments, and audit groups. Interpretation: a sudden zero or count discontinuity warns that an empty change timeline may be caused by endpoint, permission, target, or retention coverage rather than absence of changes.
charts.signalflow: data('fmc.resource.count', filter=filter('fmc.group', 'policy') or filter('fmc.group', 'deployments') or filter('fmc.group', 'audit')).sum(by=['fmc.group', 'fmc.operation', 'fmc.resource.type', 'fmc.status']).publish(label='Resources')
